title: Modules and Visibility
intro: A module is a named group of items, with its own private part. Everything inside is hidden from the outside until you mark it `pub`, and a `use` line gives a long path a short name.

coming_from.go: A Go package is both the unit of privacy and the unit of compilation. Rust splits the two: a module (`mod`) is the privacy unit, a crate the compilation unit. You declare a module with `mod` instead of putting files in a folder, and visibility is `pub` instead of a capital letter.
coming_from.kotlin: Kotlin declarations are public unless you say `private` or `internal`; Rust is the other way round, private unless `pub`. A Rust module is not a class: `private` is about the module: two types in one module can read each other's private fields. Kotlin's `internal` (the module) is `pub(crate)`, and a Rust crate is what Kotlin calls a module.
coming_from.python: A Rust module is declared with `mod`, not found by file name, and without `pub` the compiler refuses the access, where Python's `_name` is only a request. A file does not join the program by being imported: its parent has to say `mod`. Your "package" is closer to a Rust crate.
coming_from.typescript: `pub` is `export`, and an item without it cannot be named from outside. A file is not a module until its parent declares it with `mod`. `use` is `import` for names only: it does not load or run a file.
coming_from.java: A Rust module is a namespace like a package, but it is also the privacy boundary, and `pub` is closest to `public`. The default is the opposite: Java's no-modifier default is package-wide, Rust's is private to the module and its children. What Java calls a module (`module-info.java`) is a Rust crate.
coming_from.csharp: A Rust module is like a namespace, `use` is `using`, and the default is private, like a C# member. The unit of privacy is the module rather than the class. A crate is like an assembly, and `pub(crate)` is the nearest thing to `internal`.
coming_from.c: There are no headers: `mod` names a file inside a tree and does not paste text, and a crate is the translation unit. Items are private by default like `static` functions, and `pub` is what you would put in the header.
coming_from.cpp: A module is a namespace that also controls access: private items are hidden from the outside, with no `class` needed. `use` is `using`, and there are no headers or include guards, because `mod` names a node in a tree instead of pasting text.

notes: `shop::total(3)` is a path: the module name, `::`, then the item. `discount_percent` has no `pub`, so only code inside `shop` can call it, even though `main` is in the same file.
A module can be written inline, as here, or live in its own file: `mod shop;` loads `shop.rs`. The step-by-step guide to files is linked below.
`pub` is per item. Nothing is public because it is in a module, and a struct's fields are private unless each one is marked `pub`.
`use shop::total;` would let `main` write `total(3)`. It only gives a name a shortcut; it never loads a file.

gotcha.title: Private is the default
gotcha.looks_fine: Most languages you know let any code that can see a function call it: a Python module function, an unmarked top-level declaration in Kotlin or TypeScript, a C or C++ function in the same file. Here `main` and `shop` are in the same file, so calling the helper looks fine.
gotcha.rust_sees: `discount_percent` has no `pub`, so it belongs to `shop` alone. Its callers are the code inside `shop`; `main` is outside.
gotcha.why: Everything private by default means each `pub` is a decision to promise something to the outside. Whatever you leave private can be renamed or deleted without breaking anyone.

go.says: Go runs this and prints discount: 20%. The unit of privacy is the package, and this file is one package, so a lowercase name is visible to all of it. Another package would be refused (shown on this page).

kotlin.says: Kotlin refuses this too: `discountPercent` is private in `Shop`. Kotlin is public by default, so here the `private` was written on purpose.

python.says: Python prints discount: 20%. `_discount_percent` is private only by convention; nothing stops the call.
python.code:
def _discount_percent(qty: int) -> int:
    return 20 if qty >= 10 else 0


def total(qty: int) -> int:
    full = qty * 10
    return full - full * _discount_percent(qty) // 100


print("total:", total(12))
print(f"discount: {_discount_percent(12)}%")

typescript.says: TypeScript refuses this: a function in a `namespace` that is not `export`ed cannot be named from outside it.
typescript.error: main.ts(13,31): error TS2339: Property 'discountPercent' does not exist on type 'typeof Shop'.

java.says: Java runs this and prints discount: 20%. `private` means private to the top-level class, and `Shop` is nested inside `Main`, so `Main` can reach it. A separate top-level class would be refused.

csharp.says: C# refuses this too (CS0122): a member with no modifier is private, so the call from outside `Shop` is inaccessible.

c.says: C prints discount: 20%. `static` hides a function from other files, but this call is in the same file.

cpp.says: C++ prints discount: 20%. An unnamed namespace hides names from other files, but this call is in the same file, and namespaces have no access control of their own.

import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(root / "shop.py").write_text("RATE = 20\n_hidden = 'internal'\n\n\ndef total(q):\n    return q * 10\n")
(root / "shop_all.py").write_text("__all__ = ['total']\nRATE = 20\n\n\ndef total(q):\n    return q * 10\n")
(root / "extra.py").write_text("print('extra.py ran')\n")
# Two files that import each other, once with `from ... import` and once with `import`.
(root / "ping.py").write_text("from pong import g\n\n\ndef f():\n    return g()\n")
(root / "pong.py").write_text("from ping import f\n\n\ndef g():\n    return 1\n")
(root / "ping2.py").write_text("import pong2\n\n\ndef f():\n    return pong2.g()\n")
(root / "pong2.py").write_text("import ping2\n\n\ndef g():\n    return 1\n")
# A package: __init__.py re-exports a name from a file inside it.
(root / "shopkg").mkdir()
(root / "shopkg" / "__init__.py").write_text("from .rates import rate\n")
(root / "shopkg" / "rates.py").write_text("def rate():\n    return 20\n")

SHOW = "print(sorted(n for n in dir() if n in ('RATE', 'total', '_hidden')))"


def run(label, code):
    print(label)
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
    last = (out.stdout + out.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-1]
    # The error text also names a temporary folder; keep the part that is the same every time.
    print(last.split(" (consider")[0])


run("1. reach a _private name through the module", "import shop; print(shop._hidden)")
run("2. star-import: which names arrive", "from shop import *; " + SHOW)
run("3. star-import from a module with __all__", "from shop_all import *; " + SHOW)
run("4. import runs the file", "import extra")
run("5. name a module-level name that __all__ left out", "from shop_all import RATE; print(RATE)")
run("6. a cycle with `from ... import`", "import ping")
run("7. the same cycle with `import`", "import ping2; print(ping2.f())")
run("8. a package re-exports a name in __init__.py", "from shopkg import rate; print(rate())")

visibility.kt.code:
import java.io.File
import java.nio.file.Files

val root: File = Files.createTempDirectory("ktvis").toFile()

fun write(path: String, text: String) {
    val f = File(root, path)
    f.parentFile.mkdirs()
    f.writeText(text)
}

// Compiles the files with kotlinc and prints the error lines, or "ok".
fun compile(label: String, vararg args: String) {
    println(label)
    val p = ProcessBuilder("kotlinc", *args)
        .directory(root).redirectErrorStream(true).start()
    val output = p.inputStream.bufferedReader().readText()
    p.waitFor()
    val errors = output.lines().filter { ": error: " in it }
    if (errors.isEmpty()) println("  ok") else errors.forEach { println("  $it") }
}

fun main() {
    write("A.kt", """
        package shop
        private fun fileSecret() = 1
        internal fun moduleSecret() = 2
        fun open() = 3
    """.trimIndent())
    write("B.kt", """
        package shop
        fun ok() = open()
        fun bad() = fileSecret()
    """.trimIndent())
    compile("1. another file of the same package calls a private top-level function", "A.kt", "B.kt", "-d", "one")

    write("C.kt", """
        package shop
        class Outer {
            class Nested { private fun hidden() = 4 }
            fun peek() = Nested().hidden()
        }
    """.trimIndent())
    compile("2. an outer class calls a private member of its nested class", "C.kt", "-d", "two")

    write("lib/A.kt", File(root, "A.kt").readText())
    compile("3. build the package as a library", "lib/A.kt", "-d", "lib.jar")
    write("D.kt", """
        package app
        fun a() = shop.open()
        fun b() = shop.moduleSecret()
    """.trimIndent())
    compile("4. another module calls the public and the internal function", "D.kt", "-cp", "lib.jar", "-d", "three")
}
